blocks.text: The catalogue of powers tied to Narain Das’s book expands further, describing control over occult powers, the elements, hidden wealth, transformation, weather, violence, and protection from enemies.
These claims are intentionally excessive: the poet wants the reader to feel the scale of the boast, so that Narain Das appears surrounded by occult powers before he is brought low before the Guru.
By the end of the page, the occult inventory itself becomes evidence of inflation and delusion, setting up the contrast between magical display and true spiritual authority.
